PROBABILITY_YES: 42
REASON: The Reuters poll of 21-23 October 2026 had 19 of 34 economists expecting a hike, and Macklem said on 17 October that oil well above the July assumption would push inflation up and that broadening risks had grown. Soft core CPI (CPI-trim 1.8%, CPI-median 1.9%), falling employment, and the 15 of 34 forecasters still calling a hold keep a no-change outcome close to even odds.

PROBABILITY_YES: 45
REASON: The Reuters poll of 21-23 October 2026 is split almost evenly, with 19 of 34 economists expecting a 25 bp hike and 15 not forecasting one. Governor Macklem's warnings about oil-driven inflation and his "too slow to respond" language point toward a hike, while falling employment, soft core inflation and weak growth argue for a hold, so I put a hold slightly below even odds.

PROBABILITY_YES: 45
REASON: The Reuters poll of 21-23 October 2026 was split, with 19 of 34 economists expecting a 25 basis-point hike and 15 not forecasting one. Governor Macklem's warnings about oil-driven inflation and rising risk of broadening point toward a hike, while falling jobs, sub-2% core inflation and weak growth support a hold.

PROBABILITY_YES: 45
REASON: The Reuters poll split 19 to 15 in favor of a hike, and Macklem has signaled rising inflation risks, with Brent at about US$113 to $117 and the Fed and ECB tightening. Against that, core CPI measures are below 2%, employment has fallen for two months, and the Bank has historically looked through energy shocks, so a hold remains close to a coin flip.

PROBABILITY_YES: 42
REASON: The Reuters poll of 21-23 October 2026 had 19 of 34 economists expecting a 25 basis-point hike, and Governor Macklem has signalled upside inflation risks, with the Fed and ECB already tightening. Against that, core CPI measures are below 2%, employment has fallen for two months, and 15 of 34 economists still forecast no move.
